Chapter 14
Centralized Procurement
This chapter provides an overview of the SAP Ariba Central Procurement,
private cloud edition functionality and scenarios, the migration path
from a distributed SAP Supplier Relationship Management environment
with multiple backends to SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud
edition, and the integration approach for central procurement with SAP
Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and
Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA.
Large enterprises often manage multiple ERP environments. SAP Ariba Central Pro-
curement, private cloud edition allows an organization to manage procurement across
multiple SAP S/4HANA systems. This chapter outlines the capabilities, areas, and con-
figuration of SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition, beginning with an
overview, moving into the distinct process areas, and finishing with sections on config-
uration.
14.1 What Is Centralized Procurement?
In the context of procurement, centralized procurement refers to the consolidation and
central management of purchasing activities within an organization. This involves
centralizing procurement functions such as vendor management, purchase requisi-
tions, sourcing procedures, purchase orders, and contract management in a single
department or location.
A centralized procurement model means that an organization has a central purchasing
organization that handles most or all purchasing and sourcing decisions for all its
departments or business units. This team acts as a hub for strategic purchasing, making
the procurement process more efficient and streamlined across the organization.
SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is a product within SAP S/4HANA
Sourcing and Procurement. SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition rep-
resents a solution for SAP ERP customers with multiple ERP systems to manage their
procurement activities in a centralized manner while realizing the advantages of SAP’s
procurement solutions in the cloud, such as the SAP Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Mate-
rials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA. SAP
Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition represents both a transformation

path from SAP SRM and a future-ready, intelligent ERP platform for connecting to and
consuming SAP cloud solutions to seamlessly augment the process agility, capabilities,
and user experience in the overall landscape. Not only is SAP S/4HANA an ERP plat-
form, but it can also be deployed as a central procurement system integrated with mul-
tiple backend ERP systems, including older versions of SAP ERP, down to SAP ERP 6.0
EHP 6, and non-SAP systems. For simplicity, we can call these connected systems.
Many companies have found SAP SRM to be a trustworthy tool for managing supplier
relationships in the past. However, the advent of SAP S/4HANA has opened up a world
of possibilities and allowed businesses to fully realize their potential. This innovative
solution provides unparalleled agility, real-time insights, and streamlined operations,
empowering customers to achieve their goals.
With SAP’s introduction of SAP S/4HANA as the digital core and the discontinuation of
SAP SRM, for which maintenance expires in 2027, organizations are searching for ways,
solutions, and software to augment and transform their procurement processes and
ensure an orderly migration from SAP SRM. One of the most obvious challenges for a
migration from SAP SRM was ensuring like-for-like capabilities in the eventual replace-
ment system. One important value proposition of SAP SRM was its capability to act as
the central procurement hub instance in front of multiple (ERP) backends, providing
the procurement department with the capability to organize, govern, and control their
tasks from within a central environment. Procurement departments especially valued
SAP SRM’s capability to manage workload, documents, and approvals centrally, in a
procurement-focused manner, above the fray and complexities of ERP environments.
When the sunsetting of SAP SRM was announced, a natural question from the SAP SRM
customer base was, What is SAP proposing to replace its multi-ERP-management func-
tionality?
In an ideal world, every organization would only have a single ERP instance, but this is
often not the case. Many companies and organizations running SAP ERP accumulate
more than one system instance. Whether through the acquisition of another company
in which the SAP ERP environment wasn’t consolidated or a division that created its
own SAP ERP instance due to specific requirements, ERP systems in large, multina-
tional organizations sometimes proliferate. Distributed procurement landscapes with
numerous backend systems are quite common across larger companies. For example,
nearly two-thirds of large enterprises in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa with an SAP
SRM system are using it as a procurement hub in front of their diverse, multibackend
landscapes.
Merely removing SAP SRM and upgrading the ERP backends to SAP S/4HANA creates
challenges in multiple areas, but procurement is particularly impacted by this lack of
centralization in an ERP landscape. As a business function, procurement benefits from
scale and volumes. The more volume you put through a supplier or into purchasing an
item, the bigger the cost savings and efficiencies. Not only can you conduct fewer trans-
actions, saving time and effort, but you also realize the volume discount most suppli-

Managing procurement in a centralized manner also provides a platform from which
to understand your procurement activities holistically, creating a virtuous cycle
whereby each procurement iteration becomes more efficient than the last in obtaining
the goods and services your organization needs from the best supplier mix possible for
operations and to orchestrate your organization’s value creation for the marketplace.
When faced with a distributed environment, the first impulse of problem-solving IT
executives of yore was to attempt to consolidate multiple ERP systems into one. This
proved time-consuming and very complex in some cases. Master data from an
acquired company’s ERP environment and overall structure may not have matched the
receiving environment. Processes may have been different. The expense of consolida-
tion may have outweighed the upside or, from a budgeting standpoint, lacked a suffi-
cient business case to prioritize the consolidation.
SAP’s strategic direction is now focused upon cloud solutions such as SAP Ariba, SAP
Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP
S/4HANA, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Concur, leveraging SAP S/4HANA for the digital core.
SAP SRM will be supported until 2027, and much of its procurement capabilities are
being rolled into SAP S/4HANA and SAP Ariba. The capability to tie together multiple
connected systems for procurement is now available in SAP Ariba Central Procure-
ment, private cloud edition. In addition, SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud
edition allows for the coupling of more SAP Ariba solutions and SAP Ariba Direct Mate-
rials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA on top, to
further leverage cloud solutions and advanced capabilities. The diagram on the left in

Figure 14.2 includes connections to SAP Fieldglass for contingent labor management,
SAP Concur for travel and expense management, SAP Ariba/SAP Business Network,
and additional SAP S/4HANA, SAP SRM, SAP ERP, and non-SAP environments. SAP

but the options are there in the event you need to deploy further functionality. Figure

SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is a “hub” system, and it provides
organizations with a centralized platform to manage their procurement processes. This
hub system offers several advantages, including enhanced visibility and control over
procurement activities across multiple entities or subsidiaries.
By creating a centralized software system that functions across buying channels with-
out reworking them, procurement teams can pull all their disparate data sets into one
place. Cloud, on-premise SAP systems, and non-SAP systems can be integrated, and sys-
tems can be added or removed as transactions due to mergers and acquisitions occur,
without disrupting procurement operations.
When we refer to a centralized platform, we are talking about the ability to manage and
coordinate different procurement processes. Currently, there are four scenarios: requi-
sitioning, purchasing, contracting, and sourcing. A central analytical tool also enables
analyzing and monitoring procurement processes centrally.

14.3 Central Purchasing
The central purchasing scenario of SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edi-
tion provides a workplace for the purchaser to create and manage all of the purchase
documents for connected backend systems. The purchaser can monitor, display,
access, and change the purchasing documents irrespective of whether they are created
centrally by an employee using central requisitioning or in any of the connected sys-
tems. Central purchasing allows the purchaser to manage and organize the daily tasks
and workload to ensure that demands are met, sourced, and converted into purchase
orders. Once the purchase orders are released and sent to the supplier, they can then be
monitored for follow-on processes such as goods receipts and invoicing processes. In

14.3 Central Purchasing
Previously, purchase orders were generated manually or through SAP SRM in each ERP
system. These orders had to undergo an approval process, adding complexity to the
company's order management due to the multiple ERP systems. Purchase orders that
are created in the hub system or the ones that have been extracted from other con-
nected systems can be managed, as in Figure 14.9, in the Manage Purchase Orders Cen-
trally app.
The Manage Purchase Orders Centrally app provides the following main features:
 Search and filter purchase orders from different connected systems—for example,
by approval status or overdue items
 Display purchase order details
 Create purchase order manually from scratch directly in the connected system
 Open and change the purchase order directly in the connected system
Central procurement apps such as Manage POs Centrally and Process Purchase Requi-
sitions Centrally leverage a data cache of so-called proxy tables for fast searches and to
make use of the capabilities of the SAP HANA in-memory database. The original docu-
ments still reside in the backend, and data validation, checks, and enrichment happen
directly in the backend system.
SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition facilitates the integration of
attachments linked to the line-item level of a purchase order in the connected system
into central purchasing processes. This is achieved through the inclusion of the back-
end attachment's document info record in the centrally managed purchase order's
object page and the online retrieval and display of the original file from the connected
system's content server when the user selects a specific attachment.
This integration offers several advantages, including increased transparency in han-
dling line-item attachments from connected systems without the necessity of dupli-
cating the original files within the hub system. Moreover, it significantly enhances the
efficiency of purchase order output from the hub system, encompassing line-item
attachments, instead of generating output individually from each connected system.
Due to this architecture, the business document IDs remain the original IDs of the
backend document. Unlike in other integrated systems, such as SAP SRM and SAP ERP,
in which there are sometimes external and internal numbers required for the same PO
document, no separate IDs are created for external purchase requisitions or purchase
orders in central procurement and there is no need to sync number ranges or define
extensive ID mappings. Each procurement document keeps its number assigned by the
number ranges in the connected system, making them clearly identifiable to all parties,
regardless of whether they are accessing the document from within the Manage Pur-
chase Orders Centrally app or directly in the connected system.
Even in a single ERP instance, analyzing procurement activities often requires data
from disparate areas, such as materials management and accounts payables. In an

14.4 Central Sourcing
The central sourcing scenario within SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edi-
tion aims to enhance procurement efficiency by consolidating purchasing activities
across different divisions or entities within an organization. This strategy optimizes pro-
curement processes, capitalizes on collective purchasing power, and enforces standard-
ized terms. Integrating with SAP Ariba and SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for
Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA complements this approach
by providing a comprehensive platform for supplier engagement, negotiation, and con-
tract management. This integration allows organizations to extend their procurement
capabilities in the central purchasing organization, access an extensive supplier network,
and facilitate end-to-end procurement workflows that encompass sourcing, purchasing,
and supplier collaboration.
If your purchase requisitions don't have a source of supply, the central purchasing
organization may start the sourcing process to find a new supplier or contract. By using
the Manage Central RFQs app (see Figure 14.10), you can create a central request for
quotation (central RFQ) that includes those purchase requisitions without a source of
supply. There are two types of central RFQs: internal and external. The organization's
internal policy and the accepted sourcing strategy determine which type of central RFQ
to select:
 The external request is suitable for scenarios where the organization needs to source
products or services that are not readily available internally. It involves inviting
external suppliers to provide quotations and bids for the required items or services.
 The internal request is suitable for scenarios where external suppliers cannot be
involved for some reason. In that case, the central purchasing organization acts as a
supplier to submit the supplier's quotation.
You can perform the following processes in central sourcing:
 Using the Process Purchase Requisition Centrally app to create a central RFQ for pur-
chase requisitions without a source of supply
 Using the Process Purchase Requisition Centrally app to create central supplier quo-
tations in the hub system on behalf of suppliers and award the best quotation
 Creating purchase orders or central purchase contracts from the awarded central
supplier quotation

14.5 Central Purchase Contracts
The purpose of central purchasing contracts is to consolidate an organization's pro-
curement efforts by establishing standardized terms, conditions, and agreements with
suppliers. This approach streamlines the procurement process, enabling cost savings
through bulk purchasing, improving supplier relationships, and enhancing transpar-
ency and compliance. Ultimately, central purchasing contracts aim to optimize pro-
curement efficiency, reduce costs, and ensure consistent and strategic sourcing
practices across the organization.
The central purchase contracts scenario allows users to centrally create, modify, and
view contracts in the hub system. These contracts can then be distributed to connected
systems for use as a source of supply. This feature enables purchasers from different
organizational units to benefit from the negotiated terms and conditions. Central pro-
curement supports both contracts and scheduling agreements.
The configuration steps for central contracts are delineated further in Section 14.8.4.
Once these configuration steps have been completed, you can perform the following
processes in central contracts:
 Create central contracts in the central hub system via the Manage Purchase Con-
tracts app, including partial distribution of the central contract to the connected ERP
systems by company code, quantity, and/or percentage levels. At the central con-
tract item level, you can create items from imported material masters, free text

encompass comprehensive details on commodities, their quantities, and preferred

involving commodities. An awarded quotation can then serve as the foundation for

Commodity procurement is an empowering tool that allows for a user-friendly, formula-
based approach to commodity pricing applicable even for future dates, as well as for col-
lecting and managing market data rooted in derivative contract specifications (DCS).
Users can input and allocate price fixations and perform end-of-period valuations, mak-
ing it easier to oversee purchasing documents across diverse industries.
Through commodity pricing integration, as shown in Figure 14.12, it becomes feasible
to specify the commodities in use and compute item prices by incorporating the com-
modity values. Users also have the flexibility to regulate the update cycle of a specific
commodity within a central purchase contract based on individual negotiations with
the respective supplier, maintaining price data for materials over varying timeframes.
These update cycles can range from monthly and quarterly to semiannual or annual,
allowing for a more effective way to adapt to external market fluctuations in central
contract commodity prices.

For communication with the backends, OData or SOA services are used. Transactional
data, such as data in purchase requisitions, is usually transferred via asynchronous
SOA services, whereas data validation, lookups, or actions are usually performed with
synchronous OData service calls to the backends.
The needed interfaces are provided for the on-premise backends as part of an integra-
tion add-on—an additional software component that needs to be installed in the back-
end systems. This component can be installed easily in the backend and decouples the
lifecycle of the interfaces from the complex and costly lifecycle of underlying SAP ERP
or SAP S/4HANA systems.
For any business process that is spread across multiple systems, the biggest challenge
is master data. In case of procurement, this data includes materials, suppliers, and
accounting information, but also organizational information like material groups or
the purchasing organization. In the case of a central system architecture, as with any
central procurement hub system, two options can be distinguished: either all master
data, business logic, and all business objects can be consolidated into the central sys-
tem, or the workplace and business object access and workload organization can be
centralized.
Consolidation can be a tedious and arduous task. It requires a companywide under-
standing of which processes and process-specific data needs to be incorporated into
the central process flow, master data harmonization across many systems, or the cre-
ation of a mapping and data governance infrastructure. It comes with high TCO, and
consolidated processes are usually error-prone and require constant maintenance
effort, especially if the backend processes are very heterogenous. In addition, it can
slow down innovation cycles in the backends, as well as in the hub, and new features
need to be introduced synchronously in the central system and the backend.
As shown in Figure 14.23, centralization keeps the business logic and all business docu-
ments in the backends, which reduces the need to harmonize or map master data sig-
nificantly. Only very few master data elements need to be harmonized or mapped.
Mainly these are material groups and purchasing organizations. For central contract
management alone, harmonized material master data is required across the backend
landscape at this point in time.
SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition is not merely a consolidated pur-
chase order creation app but a purchasing control center, which allows customers to
(remotely) control a global, distributed, and diverse operational procurement ecosys-
tem while maintaining analytical and operational transparency and compliance.

14.9 Summary
SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition has evolved significantly since its
inception, positioning itself as the future-proof platform for orchestrating procurement
activities across diverse ERP systems. This evolution showcases not only advanced capa-
bilities surpassing those of previous SAP SRM solutions but also ongoing efforts to
enhance integration with SAP Ariba solutions or SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for
Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA, addressing process and
functionality limitations. By adopting this robust solution, customers stand to gain a
multitude of benefits.
One of the primary advantages is the streamlining of procurement operations, result-
ing in heightened efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Central procurement empowers
organizations to centralize procurement activities, fostering transparency and simpli-
fying complex procurement processes.
Furthermore, the integration potential with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network
opens new avenues for collaboration and supplier management. This synergy allows
companies to optimize supplier relationships, enhance supplier diversity, and imple-
ment strategic sourcing initiatives. The result is a more agile and responsive procure-
ment function, capable of adapting to changing market conditions and delivering
exceptional value to customers.
